properties.organization: Sindicato De Pescadores S-24 De Quintero
properties.defence_activity: Alejandro Castro defended artisan fishing and led mobilizations that sought to visualise high levels of pollution that affected the sea, land and air of Quintero and Puchuncaví.
properties.defence_activity (as published, Spanish): Alejandro Castro defendió la pesca artesanal y lideró movilizaciones que buscaban visibilizar los altos niveles de contaminación que afectaban el mar, la tierra y el aire de Quintero y Puchuncaví.
properties.event_description: A police officer at Valparaíso's 7th police station, while participating in a march against the Fishing Act at Quintero, was an unidentified police officer and called him "Alejandro Castro, we have you signed." Castro appeared hung soon after, on October 5. The police director confirmed that the fisherman had been threatened before his death. The first expert's findings have shown that Castro was killed by asphyxiation from hanging without intervention from third parties.
properties.event_description (as published, Spanish: Mientras participaba en una marcha en contra de la Ley de Pesca en Quintero, un funcionario policial de la 7° Comisaría de Valparaíso, no identificado, le gritó: "Alejandro Castro, te tenemos fichado". Castro apareció colgado poco tiempo después, el 5 de octubre. El director de la Policía de Investigaciones confirmó que el pescador había sido amenazado antes de su muerte. Las primeras pericias arrojaron que Castro falleció por asfixia por ahorcamiento sin intervención de terceros.
properties.violence_context: Alejandro Castro was secretary to one of the most widely known trade unions of artisan pesors of Valparaíso region, S-24. The main crusade was the repeal of the Fisheries Act, which, with its perspective, would lead to an indiscriminate exploitation of maritime resources and would seriously affect the labour source of the area's fishing piscains. His death was the subject of a long investigation, which confirmed his initial skills with respect to his death.
properties.violence_context (as published, Spanish): Alejandro Castro era secretario de uno de los sindicatos de pesadores artesanales de mayor notoriedad de la Región de Valparaíso, el S-24. Su principal cruzada era la derogación de la Ley de Pesca, que según su perspectiva, produciría una explotación indiscriminada de recursos marítimos y afectaría seriamente la fuente laboral de los pesqueños pesqueros de la zona. Su fallecimiento fue objeto de una larga investigación, que confirmó las pericias iniciales respecto del motivo de su muerte.

properties.event_description: Francanca Linconao was raided on January 5, 2013, as part of an investigation into the murder of the Luchsinger-Mackay marriage that occurred two days earlier. The couple died bald inside his house, located a few km from the Mashi's residence. Carabineros arrested Linconao and was held in police custody for months. He was finally acquitted as a result of his finding that he was never at his place. He got involved without concrete evidence.
properties.event_description (as published, Spanish: Francisca Linconao fue allanada el 5 de enero de 2013, en el marco de la investigación por el asesinato del matrimonio Luchsinger-Mackay, acaecido dos días antes. La pareja murió calcinada dentro de su casa, ubicada a pocos kilómetros de la residencia de la machi. Carabineros detuvo a Linconao y la Fiscalía la mantuvo en prisión preventiva durante meses. Finalmente, fue absuelta al comprobarse que nunca estuvo en el lugar de los hechos. Se le involucró sin pruebas concretas.
properties.violence_context: On 3 of 2013, a homeless marriage was attacked and killed at his house by strangers. Prosecutor's office held that Linconao assembled his assailants at his place the night before his heist. That was why she was raided, arrested and investigated, until his innocence was found twice (the trial had to be repeated and in both cases she was acquitted). A police officer said that Linconao was "of crime interest" since 2008, when he won his suit for Mount Rahue.

properties.event_description: Francisco Gómez Nadal, Spanish journalist living in Panama, was repeatedly arrested by migration authorities. The first time was in July 2010, after his leave and his passport was confiscated. He was later arrested with his wife, activist María Pilar Chato, on 27 February 2011 while covering a protest against reforms to mining law. The Government accused him of incitement and forced his marriage to leave his country.
properties.event_description (as published, Spanish: Francisco Gómez Nadal, periodista español residente en Panamá, fue detenido por las autoridades de migración en repetidas ocasiones. La primera vez fue en julio del 2010, cuando se iba a salir del país y le decomisaron el pasaporte. Luego, el 27 de febrero de 2011, fue detenido junto a su esposa, la activista María Pilar Chato, mientras cubría una protesta contra las reformas a la ley minera. El Gobierno lo acusó de instigación y obligó al matrimonio a dejar el país.
properties.violence_context: Indigenous activists, most of them from Ngäbe Buglé, had been protesting against the reform of mining law (Chorizo Act) for several days, increasing benefits from the extraction of copper, gold and silver. Journalist and activist Gómez Nadal was publicly critical of the reforms to the mining law and policies of then-President Ricardo Martinelli.
properties.violence_context (as published, Spanish): Activistas indígenas, en su mayoría de la comarca Ngäbe Buglé, llevaban varios días manifestándose contra la reforma de ley minera (Ley Chorizo), por la que se incrementan los beneficios por extracción de cobre, oro y plata. El periodista y activista Gómez Nadal era públicamente crítico de las reformas a la ley minera y de las políticas del entonces presidente Ricardo Martinelli.

properties.event_description: From 8 to 13 July 2010, workers of the Bocas Fruit Company, most of Ngäbe's ethnicity, protested at Bocas del Toro in opposition to the Government's project that intended to relax mining activity, Act 30 (Chorizo Act). On 8 July they suffered a violent police crackdown, and they fired parsnips and tear gas. There were two deaths, about 100 wounded and more than 100 detainees. The government also ordered cuts to electricity and water supply
properties.event_description (as published, Spanish: Del 8 al 13 de Julio de 2010 trabajadores de la bananera Bocas Fruit Co., en su mayoría de la etnia Ngäbe, protestaron en Bocas del Toro en rechazo al proyecto del Gobierno que pretendía flexibilizar la actividad minera, la Ley 30 (Ley Chorizo). El 8 de julio sufrieron una represión violenta por parte de la policía, que disparó perdigones y gases lacrimógenos. Hubo dos muertes, un centenar de heridos y más de cien detenidos. Además, el gobierno ordenó cortes del suministro eléctrico y de agua po
properties.violence_context: The banana union and indigenous and environmental activists demand that Act 30 be repealed, an executive project that was unconditionally approved by the National Assembly and with a bad view of the Supreme Court of Justice, that relaxed mining conditions in Panama and, inter alia, eliminated the obligation to conduct an environmental impact assessment.
properties.violence_context (as published, Spanish): El sindicato bananero exigió junto a indígenas y activistas ambientales la derogación de la Ley 30, un proyecto del Ejecutivo aprobado de forma inconstitucional por la Asamblea Nacional y con la vista gorda de la Corte Suprema de Justicia, que flexibilizaba las condiciones de la minería en Panamá y, entre otras cosas, eliminaba la obligatoriedad de evaluaciones de impacto ambiental.

After 16 days after closing the track, anti-riot units destroyed the camp, and with tear-gas attacks on protesters and arrested about 20 people. The mining company provided the National Police with helicopters to conduct the operation.

Luego de 16 días del cierre de la vía, unidades antimotines destruyeron el campamento, atacaron con gases lacrimógenos a los protestantes y arrestaron aproximadamente a 20 personas. La empresa minera facilitó a la Policía Nacional los helicópteros para llevar a cabo la operación.

In addition to the Petawilla Copper Project (Petawilla Copper Ltd) located in the province of Coclé, in the Eastern Centre of Panama. The loss of forest and the pollution caused by mining from the beginning of March 2009 of the San Juan and Melejones River have been leading peasants and indigenous people to protest and install the camp.

properties.event_description: The Eleta Group took an island, with an included town, for a mega-tourist-residential luxury. He built an airport, houses, seabirds, hotels and stripped his local lands for growing, hunting and up to the sea. When the inhabitants began to protest, they responded with repression and a criminal complaint to 37 people from the Pedro González Committee for Defence, for which several were held.

Cuando los habitantes comenzaron a protestar, respondieron con represión y una denuncia penal a 37 personas del Comité Pro Defensa de Pedro González, por la que varios estuvieron presos.
properties.violence_context: A residential and tourist project swept up with the spaces and lives of a community with more than 300 inhabitants in a forgotten paradise of the Las Perlas Archipelago called Pedro González. A dubious title of property, police repression, prosecution and a broken town forever.
properties.violence_context (as published, Spanish): Un proyecto turístico-residencial arrasó con los espacios y la vida de una comunidad de más de 300 habitantes en un paraíso olvidado del archipiélago Las Perlas llamado Pedro González. properties.event_description: Some men who identified themselves as members of the group called The Pelusas came to his place and told him to "stand still" and stop talking about "defending the earth." They were also members of the Fac's dissidences (Dagoberto Ramos column) to seek him at his mother's place but he was missing. Likewise, they have circulated leaflets of guerrillas and criminal gangs with them as an "enemy of development" and as an obstacle to their passing through Nasa.
properties.event_description (as published, Spanish: Unos hombres que se identificaron como miembros del grupo llamado Los Pelusos llegaron a buscarlo a su casa para decirle que "se quede quieto" y deje de hablar de "defender la tierra". También fueron miembros de las disidencias de las Farc, (columna Dagoberto Ramos) a buscarlo a casa de su madre, pero él no se encontraba. Igualmente han circulado panfletos de guerrilla y bandas criminales donde lo señalan de "enemigo del desarrollo" y de impedir el paso de estos grupos por territorio Nasa.
properties.violence_context: Following the peace process with the Farms several groups have come to Florida, in Valle del Cauca, to attempt to exercise control in areas of the Territory. There have been harassment, threats to the population and tensions as the Nasa community prevents the cultivation of marijuana and coca and the passing of armed groups through their paths. The construction of the Pacific-Orinocchik Connecting road puts at risk the moors of Las TINajas and Las Hermosas and to Nasa Kwesx Yu Kiwe.
properties.violence_context (as published, Spanish): Después del proceso de paz con las Farc varios grupos han llegado a Florida, en el Valle del Cauca, para intentar ejercer control en zonas del territorio. La construcción de la carretera Conexión Pacífico-Orinoquía pone en peligro los páramos de Las Tinajas y Las Hermosas y al resguardo Nasa Kwesx Yu Kiwe.
